The first of three 2026 NFL games in London arrives in Week 4 on Sunday, with the Indianapolis Colts facing the Washington Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Dave Pasch, Kurt Warner, and Jason Kelce will provide the commentary for NFL Network (9:30 a.m. ET).

With Joe Davis having MLB postseason duties for Fox, Kenny Albert steps in as the NFL play-by-play announcer alongside Greg Olsen. They will call Sunday’s game between the Dallas Cowboys and Houston Texans (1 p.m. ET).

Like Davis, Adam Amin will call MLB postseason games for Fox, and veteran play-by-play broadcaster Tim Brando will fill in to join Drew Brees in the booth when the New York Jets and Chicago Bears battle on Sunday (1 p.m. ET).

The Fox A-team of Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady will call Sunday’s game between the Los Angeles Rams and Philadelphia Eagles (1 p.m. ET).

At CBS, Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt will follow up a wild Rio game broadcast to call Sunday’s clash between two unbeaten AFC West teams in the Kansas City Chiefs and Las Vegas Raiders.

item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball revealed the television schedule and scenarios for the 2026 postseason’s Wild Card Series on Sunday. Details have since emerged about the announcing crews that will call the games across NBC platforms.

As was the case during the regular season, local analysts will be in the booth to give each broadcast a familiar voice for each team. Additionally, each broadcast will feature one “Inside the Pitch” analyst.

The Wild Card Series is a best-of-three, so it’s unclear which, if any, series will go three games into Thursday. But here’s a look at the setup for Tuesday and Wednesday (all times are Eastern):

Philadelphia Phillies at Atlanta Braves (2 p.m., NBC/Peacock)

Matt Vasgersian (play-by-play), John Kruk (analyst), C.J. Nitkowski (analyst), Joey Votto (“Inside the Pitch” analyst), Ashley ShahAhmadi (reporter)

The energetic Vasgersian has called many postseason games in his career and has been a major presence on MLB Network for 17 years.

Kruk brings a one-of-a-kind, unapologetically honest personality to the Phillies broadcast booth, and Philadelphia fans will be happy to hear him on the call as he goes through the same emotions they do during a postseason series. Nitkowski became the primary color analyst for the Braves in 2024.

Votto quickly became a star as an “Inside the Pitch” analyst for NBC in his first year working television after a decorated MLB career that included winning the 2021 NL MVP award.

Chicago White Sox at Houston Astros (5 p.m., Peacock/NBCSN)

Tom McCarthy (play-by-play), Steve Stone (analyst), Geoff Blum (analyst), Adam Ottavino (“Inside the Pitch” analyst), Britney Eurton (reporter)

McCarthy is a versatile play-by-play announcer that fans may recognize from NFL and March Madness broadcasts for CBS. And he’s one of the top regional sports network announcers, working alongside Kruk in the Philadelphia booth.

Stone has been a longtime color commentator for the White Sox, just like Blum has been for the Astros.

Ottavino retired from the majors last year after a lengthy career as an effective relief pitcher, and he’s already made himself very busy as an analyst for NBC, ESPN, and YES Network.

Boston Red Sox at New York Yankees (8 p.m., NBC/Peacock)

Jason Benetti (play-by-play), Lou Merloni (analyst), Joe Girardi (analyst), Anthony Rizzo (“Inside the Pitch” analyst), Caroline Pineda (reporter)

Benetti is a fan favorite and is the voice of Sunday Night Baseball as the NBC lead play-by-play announcer. It’s certainly no surprise that NBC assigned him to the Red Sox-Yankees series.

Red Sox fans are extremely familiar with Merloni, as are Yankees fans with Girardi.

Rizzo has been superb as an analyst for NBC and Netflix, and two years ago, he was playing postseason games for the Yankees.

Chicago Cubs at San Diego Padres (10 p.m., Peacock/NBCSN)

Dave Flemming (play-by-play), Jim Deshaies (analyst), Mark Grant (analyst), Clayton Kershaw (“Inside the Pitch” analyst), John Fanta (reporter)

Flemming gets the late-night game, a role he carried for years as a college sports play-by-play voice for ESPN, and now for NBC. He’s also been a play-by-play announcer for the San Francisco Giants for more than two decades.

Deshaies and Grant make for an incredible pairing. “J.D.” brings his dry humor, witty commentary, and sharp analysis to Cubs broadcasts. And “Mud” is one of the most entertaining analysts in the sport, working alongside Don Orsillo to form a Padres booth that Awful Announcing readers voted No. 1 in MLB in consecutive years.

Kershaw brings an excellent perspective to pitching after just wrapping up a remarkable career that will land him in Cooperstown.

—

ESPN Radio provides nationwide coverage for every round of the postseason, including the Wild Card, Division Series, League Championship Series, and the World Series. Here are the announcer rundowns for the Wild Card round:

Phillies-Braves: Dave O’Brien, Jessica Mendoza

White Sox-Astros: Roxy Bernstein, Gregg Olson

Red Sox-Yankees: Michael Kay, Eduardo Perez, Tim Kurkjian

Cubs-Padres: Jon Sciambi, Doug Glanville

In primetime, No. 23 Texas A&M and No. 10 LSU will meet in Baton Rouge, with Joe Tessitore and Jesse Palmer calling the action for ABC at 7:30 p.m. ET. The NFL goes to Brazil in Week 3 with the Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys facing off at Rio de Janeiro’s Maracanã Stadium (despite field concerns). Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt will be on the call for CBS.

After a high-scoring opening week, several intriguing matchups are on the way in Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season.

The Week 2 action gets started with a Thursday Night Football showdown between the Detroit Lions and Buffalo Bills at the brand-new Highmark Stadium. Al Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit will be on the call for Prime Video.

Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt will return for their second game together on CBS when the Pittsburgh Steelers take on the New England Patriots in Foxborough.

The Fox “America’s Game of the Week” will feature an NFC East matchup between the Washington Commanders and Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady will be in the booth for Fox.

Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth will have the NBC broadcasting duties when the Indianapolis Colts and Kansas City Chiefs battle at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday Night Football.

The New York Giants are coming off an impressive win to kick off the John Harbaugh era, while the Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams were steamrolled by the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. Joe Buck and Troy Aikman will call a storyline-filled Giants-Rams matchup for ESPN/ABC on Monday Night Football at SoFi Stadium.

item.content:encoded:
The NFL season kicks off with a wild Week 1 slate that even features a Wednesday night game, as well as a Thursday night game in Australia (where it’s technically a Friday morning game).

Wednesday will bring the NFL season opener in a Super Bowl rematch between the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks. It will be televised on NBC (8:20 p.m. ET) with Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth on the call (and it will be interesting to see how they address the relationship between Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel and former NFL insider Dianna Russini).

That’s followed by the San Francisco 49ers taking on the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday night (8:35 p.m. ET) in Melbourne (10:35 a.m. local time). Noah Eagle and Luke Kuechly will be in the booth — and NFL insider Tom Pelissero will make his debut as a Netflix sideline reporter — for what’s one of five Netflix games on the 2026 NFL schedule.

Sunday will have 13 games, featuring eight games in the early window (1 p.m. ET) and four games in the 4:25 p.m. ET window before Sunday Night Football between the Dallas Cowboys and New York Giants, which will again have Tirico and Collinsworth on the NBC broadcast.

With CBS Sports placing Tony Romo on leave after his recent OWI arrest, J.J. Watt takes over as the color commentator alongside Jim Nantz. They will make their debut as a duo for the Week 1 contest between the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings (4:25 p.m. ET).

And with Watt joining Nantz, color commentator Ross Tucker moves up to the No. 2 CBS booth and will work alongside Ian Eagle. They will call one of Week 1’s best matchups, with the Houston Texans hosting the Buffalo Bills (1 p.m. ET).

The lead Fox team of Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady will call an NFC East duel between the Washington Commanders and Philadelphia Eagles (4:25 p.m. ET).

The 2026 college football season got underway with Week 0, but things really kick into gear in the coming days with Week 1.

There will be FBS games from Thursday through Monday, led by a jam-packed slate on Saturday.

The Fox “Big Noon” game will feature defending champion Indiana hosting North Texas, with Gus Johnson and Joel Klatt on the call.

ESPN’s top broadcast team of Chris Fowler and Kirk Herbstreit will call the first game of the Lane Kiffin era at LSU against Dabo Swinney and Clemson on Saturday night (7:30 p.m. ET).

No. 2 Oregon will host Boise State with Brad Nessler and new lead analyst Charles Davis providing the broadcast duties for CBS on Saturday (3:30 p.m. ET).

Sunday night will feature two high-profile games. Wisconsin and Notre Dame face off at Lambeau Field, with Dan Hicks and Jason Garrett in the booth for NBC. And Sean McDonough and Greg McElroy will have the ESPN on ABC call of Louisville-Ole Miss in Nashville.

Week 1 will wrap up with Dave Pasch and Dusty Dvoracek calling SMU-Florida State for ESPN on Monday night (7:30 p.m. ET).

item.content:encoded:
The television schedule for the 2026 NCAA Tournament men’s Final Four was revealed on Sunday after the conclusion of the Elite Eight games.

It’s rather simple for this round of games.

Each Final Four game will be available on TNT Sports networks: TBS, TNT, and truTV. Additionally, the games will stream on NCAA March Madness Live and HBO Max (The games are *not* available on Paramount+ due to not being televised on CBS).

And each game will have the top March Madness broadcast crew of Ian Eagle, Bill Raftery, and Grant Hill on the call. Tracy Wolfson will provide the sideline reporting, and Gene Steratore will serve as a rules analyst.

The Final Four action begins with No. 3 seed Illinois vs. No. 2 seed Connecticut at 6:09 p.m. ET.

That’s followed by No. 1 seed Michigan vs. No. 1 seed Arizona, which does not have an officially scheduled tip time. The Michigan-Arizona tip time will be dependent on when the Illinois-UConn game concludes. Most likely, Michigan-Arizona will begin some time between 8:30 and 9 p.m. ET, unless Illinois-UConn goes into overtime or features rather lengthy stoppages.

Illinois reached the Final Four for the first time in 21 years, while UConn advanced for the third time in four years with an unbelievable win to stun top-seeded Duke. The Michigan-Arizona game will be a matchup of two juggernauts and should feel like a national championship game.

Saturday, April 4

(3) Illinois vs. (2) UConn | 6:09 p.m. | TBS/TNT/truTV; Ian Eagle, Bill Raftery, Grant Hill, Tracy Wolfson, Gene Steratore

(1) Michigan vs. (1) Arizona | Following Game 1 | TBS/TNT/truTV; Ian Eagle, Bill Raftery, Grant Hill, Tracy Wolfson, Gene Steratore

item.content:encoded:
Super Bowl LX is finally here. Here’s everything you need to know about how to watch or listen to Super Bowl LX on Sunday, Feb. 8, 2026, plus NBC Sports, ESPN, Westwood Radio, and local radio broadcasting plans. (All times are Eastern).

Super Bowl LX | Levi’s Stadium, Santa Clara, CA

New England Patriots (AFC No. 2 seed, 14-3, 3-0 postseason) vs. Seattle Seahawks (NFC No. 1 seed, 14-3, 2-0 postseason)
Kickoff is scheduled for 6:30 p.m. ET, broadcast live on NBC and streamed exclusively on Peacock, with coverage also available via Telemundo, NFL+, and live TV streaming services like YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, and DirecTV. There is no altcast.

NBC Sports Super Bowl LX commentators

Super Bowl broadcasters
Game commentators: Mike Tirico, Cris Collinsworth
Sideline reporters: Melissa Stark, Kaylee Hartung
Rules analyst: Terry McAulay

NBC Super Bowl LX Pregame Show commentators
Main Set: Maria Taylor, Jac Collinsworth, Noah Eagle, Tony Dungy, Jason Garrett, Rodney Harrison, and Devin McCourty
Contributors: Mike Florio, Chris Simms, Steve Kornacki, Matthew Berry, Kit Hoover

NBC Super Bowl Sunday programming schedule
Milan Cortina Winter Olympics (live): 7 a.m.
Road to the Super Bowl: Noon
Super Bowl LX Pregame Show: 1 p.m.
Super Bowl LX: 6:30 p.m.
NBC postgame show, 10 p.m. approx, including Lombardi Trophy presentation, game highlights, and analysis
Primetime in Milan: 10:45 p.m.

Telemundo Super Bowl LX commentators
Game commentators: Miguel Gurwitz and Rolando Cantú
Reporter: Diego Arrioja
Studio: Adriana Monsalve, Lindsay Casinelli,  Jessica Carrillo, Carlos Adyan, Verónica Rodríguez, Pablo Mariño, Alejandro Berry, Sofía Vergara (special guest), Julio Vaqueiro

Telemundo Super Bowl Sunday programming schedule
Camino al Super Bowl pre-game show, 1 p.m.
Super Bowl LX 6:30 p.m.
Telemundo postgame show, 10:30 p.m. approx.

Musical Performances
Opening Ceremony: Green Day
National Anthem performed by Charlie Puth
‘America the Beautiful’ performed by Brandi Carlile
‘Lift Every Voice and Sing’ performed by Coco Jones
Apple Music Super Bowl Halftime Show performed by Bad Bunny

Super Bowl LX radio broadcasts 

Westwood One Radio
English-language radio broadcast of Super Bowl LX on Westwood One Sports app, SiriusXM, NFL+, and via the NFL App.
Game commentators: Kevin Harlan, Kurt Warner
Sideline reporter: Laura Okmin
Rules analyst: Gene Steratore
Studio: Scott Graham and Ryan Harris

Westwood One Radio Super Bowl Sunday programming schedule
Super Bowl Preview with Scott Graham, Ross Tucker, and Kurt Warner: Noon
Super Bowl Insider with Scott Graham, Ryan Harris, and Ian Rapoport: 1 p.m.
Super Bowl Tailgate Show with Mike Golic and Mike Golic Jr.: 2 p.m.
Super Sunday Pregame Show: 4:00 p.m.
Super Bowl LX Game Broadcast: 5:00 p.m.
Super Bowl LX: 6:30 p.m.

Entravision Radio
Spanish language radio broadcast of Super Bowl LX (availability here)
Game commentators: Ricardo Celis, Tony Nuñez

New England Patriots radio
The Patriots’ local English-language radio broadcast airs on 98.5 The Sports Hub and its affiliates, as well as on SiriusXM channel 821.
Broadcast: Bob Socci, Scott Zolak, Marc Cappello

Seattle Seahawks radio
The Seahawks’ local radio broadcast is on Seattle Sports 710AM, KIRO Newsradio 97.3 FM, other affiliates, the Seahawks Mobile App, and SiriusXM 226.
English Broadcast: Steve Raible, Dave Wyman, and Jen Mueller (sideline reporter)

Super Bowl LX international broadcasts

ESPN Australia and New Zealand: Chris Fowler, Dan Orlovsky, Louis Riddick, and Lindsey Thiry
ESPN Brazil: Fernando Nardini, Paulo Antunes, and Conrado Giulietti
ESPN Latin America: Eduardo Varela, Pablo Viruega, Ciro Procuna and John Sutcliffe
